full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: This appeal by the State is against the judgment and order dated February 9, 1995 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 799 of 1994 quashing the proceedings of Ramna P.S. Case No. 31(6) of 1993 (corresponding DAB GR Case No. 70 of 1993) of the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. The aforementioned Ramna P.S. Case No. 31(6) of 1993 was registered under sections 420, 409 and 471 of the Penal Code as well as under Section 5(2) of the Anti-Corruption Act, 1947 (Act II of 1947). The aforementioned Ramna P.S. Case No. 31(6) of 1993 was registered on the lodging of the FIR on 13.6.1993 by an Inspector of the Bureau of Anti-corruption alleging that the Respondent, who was petitioner before the High Court Division, while serving as Assistant Adjutant of Answers was declared surplus in the light of the report of the Enam Committee and thereupon he was nominated for absorption in the National Board of Revenue either as Income Tax Inspector or Customs Inspector and ultimately he was absorbed as Inspector in the Directorate of Customs Intelligent and investigation at Khulna and the Respondent joined at the Customs office at Khulna; that lateron it was detected that the Respondent obtained the job on the basis of false certificate of B.Com (Pass) Examination of Tularam Government College, Narayangonj and thus practiced fraud upon the Government in obtaining the job. 

 "Seeing the provisions of Section 5-A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 read with section 167(5) of the Code of Criminal procedure we are of the view that the aforesaid Criminal Proceeding lost its legal force inasmuch as the investigation agency failed to submit the charge-sheet within 180 days from the date of institution of the case. Since in the special law, special period of limitation has been fixed for submission of police report and since the law requires that if the investigating agency failed to submit the police report within the stipulated time, the proceeding should be stopped and the accused should be released. Considering the above, we are of the view that the present criminal proceeding against the petitioner lost its legal force after 180 days from the date of institution of the case, that is, on 13-6-93. In this view of the matter, we find that the impugned proceeding is liable to be quashed". 

 4. The learned Additional Attorney General submits that the High Court Division was in serious error in quashing the proceedings of the case in question on the wrong view of the law in that provision for stopping the proceeding and releasing the accused for non-completion of investigation within certain specified time was amended prior to the institution of the case on 13.6.1993 and as such the case so initiated against the Respondent would be governed by the law as was on 13.6.1993. The learned Additional Attorney General continues that High Court Division totally failed to notice that by the Code of Criminal Procedure (Second Amendment) Act, 1992, sub-section 5 of section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) was substituted and thereby the previous provision of stopping investigation and releasing the accused for not completing the investigation within the specified time was deleted and as such the order of the High Court Division quashing the proceeding of the Ramna P.S. Case No. 31(6)93 against the Respondent was wrong and not sustainable in law. It has also been submitted that although in section 5A (inserted in 1987) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 there is mention of sub-section 5 of Section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which at the relevant time provided for that investigation is to be completed against the accused by the specified time mentioned herein, i.e. 180 days but there is nothing in the said section if investigation is not completed by the time specified in the section what will happen or in other words would the Court pass an order releasing the accused and stopping the proceeding and that being the position of law the High Court Division ought not have quashed the proceedings as sought for by the Respondent. It may be mentioned sub-section 5 was initially inserted in section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the Code of Criminal Procedure (2nd Amendment) Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. 24 of 1982) and the newly inserted subsection 5 was as follows: 

 7. In between 1982 and 1992 there has been amendment in the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 upon assertion of section 5A, provision whereof reads as: 

 8. The learned Additional Attorney General submits that when the proceeding was initiated against the Respondent provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was that in case investigation of a case within the specified time of 180 days is not completed the accused would be released on bail and that if the accused is not released on bail the Court shall record reason for that and that being the position of law i.e. there being no provision for releasing an accused and stopping the proceedings for not completing the investigation of a case within the specified time the High Court Division was wrong in quashing the proceeding of the case on the view as the investigation was not completed within the specified time, the proceeding against the Respondent lost its legal force after the time specified in section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. The learned Additional Attorney General further submits that provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is to be read in section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act. keeping in mind the provision of said sub-section at the relevant time i.e. when the proceeding initiated or that as regard the pending proceeding the position thereof and the position of law at the material time i.e. if law which is procedural is amended and thereby stopping of proceeding for non-completion of investigation ceased to be the law and that in the light of amended provision of law if investigation of the case could not be completed within the specified time, then the Court would be required to make order as contemplates by the amended provision of law i.e. as per provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as was on the date of initiation of the proceeding, i.e. 13. 6.1993, in respect of the Respondent. It was also the contention of the learned Additional Attorney General that as regard the procedural law an accused has no vested right and the proceeding against the accused would be proceeded as per pro-vision of law as on the date of initiation of the proceeding as well as on the date of trial. In that regard the learned Additional Attorney General has referred to the case of A.K.M. Azizul Islam and another Vs. State reported in 49 DLR (AD) 115 wherein it has been observed "The provisions of section 167 CrPC being a procedural law, there being no express provision for its prospective operation, shall operate retrospectively. Thus, in view of the provisions of the amended section 167 CrPC the petitioners did not acquire any legal right of claiming stoppage of investigation and getting themselves released from the case under the repealed law". 

 9. He has also referred to the case of Government of Bangladesh Vs. Shah Alam reported in (1995) 3 BLT (AD), 172 wherein it has been observed" …….. with the amendment of section 167 Cr. P.C. by Act 42 of 1992 as referred to above, the time limit for conclusion of investigation was done away with and the amendment being in respect of a procedural law, we think there was no legal difficulty with the police to continue with the investigation of the case after the aforesaid amendment came into force on first November, 1992………." and to the case of Abdul Wadud Vs. the State reported in (1995) 3 BLT (AD) 236 (same case has also been reported in 48 DLR (AD) 6) wherein it has been observed "The effect of repeal of the old provision followed by it's reenactment will be that in the pending cases the new procedural law will apply because as a general rule alteration in the form of procedure are retrospective in character unless there is some contrary provision in the enactment". In the said very case it has been observed that because of the repeal of the old provision of procedural law followed by re-enactment the new procedural law will be applicable in the pending cases although instituted when the old provision was in force and the pending cases are to be governed by the new procedure under the amended law. The proceeding against the Respondent was initiated upon lodging of FIR on 13.6.1993. Act that time the provision in section 167(5) Cr. P. C as quoted hereinbefore (enacted by Act 42 of 1992) and under the new enacted sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr. P.C. in case investigation could not be concluded within the time specified in the sub-section from the date of receipt of the information relating to the commission of offence or the order of the Magistrate for such investigation, in that state of the matter the Magistrate empowered to take cognizance of an offence or to make the order for investigation may, if the offence to which the investigation relates is not punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment exceeding 10 years, release the accused on bail to the satisfaction of such Magistrate and the Court of Sessions may, if the offence to which investigation relates is punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment exceeding 10 years release the accused on bail to the satisfaction of such Court and if the accused is not released on bail by the Court of Magistrate or by the Court of sessions in that case the Magistrate or the Court of Session shall record the reason for not releasing the accused on bail. 

 10. The learned Counsel for the Respondent upon referring to the provision of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (Act XL of 1958), as amended by inserting section 5A by the Criminal Law Amendment (Amendment) Ordinance, 1987 (Ordinance III of 1987) (lateron enacted as Act 13 of 1987) submits that in the said provision of law i.e. section 5A period for completion of investigation of a case under the Criminal Law Amendment Act is 180 days and the said period for completion of investigation has been specified upon reference to the provision of sub-section 5 of Section 167 Cr. P.C and as such in case of non-completion of investigation by the specified time, consequence as was provided in sub-section 5 of section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in 1987 would be applicable to the case governed by the provision of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and not by the provision of sub-section 5 of Section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure subsequently amended. Upon referring to section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 the learned Counsel for the Respondent submits that in 1987 when the said section was inserted in the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 the provision of sub-section 5 of Section 167 Cr.P.C. was that in case investigation of a case is not completed within the time specified in the said sub-section, further investigation into of the case shall be stopped and that as per provision of sub-section 7 of section 167 Cr. P.C. the accused if in custody shall be released forth with. The sum total of the submission of the learned Counsel of the Respondent is that since there is reference of sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr.P.C. in the newly enacted section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 in 1987, the case of the Respondent is to be governed by the provision of sub-section 5 and sub-section 7 of section 167 Cr. P.C. as was in 1987 and not as per the provision of sub-section 5 of Section 167 Cr. P.C. as in 1993 i.e. not as per the provision of law enacted by the Act 42 of 1992 (published in the gazette on 1.11.1992). The case against the Respondent was initiated on June 13, 1993 and at that time the provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr.P.C. as enacted on 1.11.1992 and till today as regard cases investigation whereof not completed within the time specified then the accused of such a case would be released on bail but the proceeding as against the accused would not be stopped. It may be mentioned by the Act 42 of 1992 provision of sub-section 7 of section 167 Cr. P.C. was deleted. By the Act No. 42 of 1992 provision in sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr. P.C. as to stopping of the investigation of a case for non-completion of investigation within the time prescribed in sub-section was deleted and in place thereof provision for releasing the accused on bail was enacted. In the instant case after the initiation of the case the Respondent appeared before the Court and obtained bail. The law is settled now that in respect of procedural law an accused has no vested right. This being the position of law even if there is mention of sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr. P.C. in section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 relating to time for completion of investigation but for that it can not be read in section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act that as investigation was not completed within the time prescribed in the said section i.e. section 5A, further investigation in the case against the Respondent is to be stopped, which amounts to non-existence of any proceeding against the Respondent, since when the case against the Respondent was initiated in June 13, 1993 the provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr.P.C. was not the one as was in 1987 when there has been amendment in the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and there was insertion of section 5A in the said Act. Since the case quashing of which prayed for and allowed by the High Court Division was initiated in June, 1993, the said case unquestionably is to be governed by the provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr. P.C. as was then. On June 13, 1993 when the case was initiated against the Respondent there was no provision in sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr. P.C. for stopping further investigation of the case against the Respondent. 

 11. In the background of the discussions made hereinbefore we are of the view the High Court Division was in serious error in quashing the proceeding of the case against the Respondent on the view as investigation of the case was not completed within the time specified in section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, further investigation of the said case in view of the provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr. P.C. an order stopping the further investigation into the case against the respondent should have been passed by the Court and he should have been released. The learned Counsel for the Respondent could not show that there is any provision in the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 for stopping further investigation of a case investigation whereof could not be finished within the time specified in section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (the Act) and that there is provision for releasing the accused for non-completion of investigation of the case against him within the time specified as in section 5A of the Act. Since provision for stopping further investigation of a case as investigation thereof could not be completed within the time specified in section 5A of the Act was not in sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr. P.C. when the case was initiated against the Respondent, as such the contention of the leaned Counsel for the Respondent that High Court Division was not in error in quashing the proceeding of the case against the Respondent taking the view as the investigation was not completed within time specified in section 5A of the Act the Court was required to make an order stopping the further investigation of the case and to release the Respondent, but the Court below have not done so. The contention of the learned Counsel since investigation of the case was not completed within the time specified in section 5A of the Act, the proceeding against the Respondent "lost its legal force" is not correct as except in sub-section 5 of section 167 of the Cr. P.C. as was in 1987 there was or is no provision in any other law for stopping investigation of a case against the Respondent because of non-completion of investigation by the time specified in the said sub-section, but as on the date when the case was initiated against the Respondent there was no provision in sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr. P.C. for stopping investigation for non-completion of investigation within specified time there was no occasion for stopping the investigation in the case initiated against the Respondent or in other words to hold because of non-completion of investigation within the specified time as in sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr. P.C. the case against the Respondent "lost its legal force" as held by the High Court Division. The learned Counsel for the Respondent referred to the cases reported in 2 BLC (AD) 87, 14 BLD (AD) 143, 52 DLR (AD) 51, and 51 DLR (AD) 142. The law enunciated in the aforesaid cases has no relevancy to the point involved in the case as well as for making decision as regard the question of law involved in the instant case. 

 12. The learned Counsel for the Respondent upon referring to the provision of Article 35(1) of the Constitution has submitted that the Respondent is to be dealt with as per the law as is in force at the relevant time i.e. as per the provision of section 5A of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. The provision of Article 35(1) provides that a person would be convicted for violation of the law that was in force at the time of commission of the offence. In the instant case the Respondent is being prosecuted for the violation of the law as was in force at the time of commission of offence. Hence the contention made upon referring to Article 35(1) of the Constitution is of no merit. In section 5A of the Act although there is provision for completion of investigation within the specified time, but there is nothing in the said section in case investigation is not completed within the time specified therein what consequence would follow. For the consequence that would follow for non-completion of investigation within specified time one is to look into sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr.P.C. as regard the cases of instant category and there is nothing in sub-section 5 of Section 167 Cr.P.C. (as enacted on 1-11-1992) that in case of non-completion of investigation within specified time, further investigation would be stopped. The learned Counsel for the Respondent has placed reliance on the provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr.P.C. for the purpose of consequence that would follow in case of non-completion of investigation by the time specified in section 5A of the Act. To substantiate the aforesaid contention it has been contended by the leaned Counsel for the Respondent that the Respondent is to be governed by the provision of sub-section 5 and sub-section 7 of section 167 Cr.P.C. as was in 1987 i.e. when section 5A was inserted in the Act because of the provision of Article 35(1) of the Constitution. The contention so made is not legally well founded since proceeding was initiated against the Respondent on June 13, 1993 and as such he would be governed by the provision of sub-section 5 of section 167 Cr.P.C. as was at that time and no other provision of law. Sub-section 7 of Section 167 Cr. P.C. was not in the statute when the case was initiated against the Respondent.
